name: Editing policy files directly
purpose: Change the raw keys and values of a policy file, and bring registry files in or out of it.

layers.name: Dialog windows and their reactions
layers.summary: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.
layers.detail: What a person sees and enters in the program's windows, and the routines that answer each click, selection and window event before handing the choices to the policy code.

layers.name: Policy definitions and files
layers.summary: Reads the administrative template and comment files, joins them into policies, categories and products, and holds the data shapes those steps use.

layers.name: Program setup and settings
layers.summary: Settings that tell Windows how to run the program and the helper that keeps the person's choices between runs.

rules.headline: In the section dialog, OK does nothing
rules.detail: In the section dialog, OK does nothing until User or Computer is chosen; then it returns that section and closes.

rules.headline: Number entered for a registry value is limited…
rules.summary: A number entered for a registry value is limited to 0 to 4,294,967,295 for a 32-bit value and to 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for a 64-bit…
rules.detail: A number entered for a registry value is limited to 0 to 4,294,967,295 for a 32-bit value and to 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for a 64-bit value.

rules.headline: Registry prefix box in the export dialog starts…
rules.summary: The registry prefix box in the export dialog starts as HKEY_CURRENT_USER\ when the user policy source is being edited and HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\ otherwise.
rules.detail: The registry prefix box in the export dialog starts as HKEY_CURRENT_USER\ when the user policy source is being edited and HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\ otherwise. It can be changed, and the export uses the text in the box unchecked.

rules.headline: New registry value dialog offers the types String
rules.summary: The new registry value dialog offers the types String, Expandable string, List of strings, 32-bit DWord and 64-bit QWord, and starts on String.
rules.detail: The new registry value dialog offers the types String, Expandable string, List of strings, 32-bit DWord and 64-bit QWord, and starts on String. Confirming returns the typed name, unchecked and possibly empty, with the chosen type; cancelling returns neither.

rules.headline: When a REG file is chosen…
rules.summary: When a REG file is chosen and the prefix is empty, the prefix is guessed from the file; if the file holds default values
rules.detail: When a REG file is chosen and the prefix is empty, the prefix is guessed from the file; if the file holds default values, the person is warned "This REG file contains data for default values, which cannot be applied to all policy sources."

rules.headline: Only files of type *.reg are offered…
rules.detail: Only files of type *.reg are offered by the file chooser when browsing for the REG file.

rules.headline: Pressing Escape closes the section dialog as cancelled
rules.detail: Pressing Escape closes the section dialog as cancelled.

rules.headline: Raw policy file editor lists keys in alphabetical…
rules.summary: The raw policy file editor lists keys in alphabetical order ignoring case, each followed by its sub-keys indented, then its values in alphabetical order
rules.detail: The raw policy file editor lists keys in alphabetical order ignoring case, each followed by its sub-keys indented, then its values in alphabetical order; a value with an empty name (the marker that keeps an empty key) is not listed.

rules.headline: When Delete is confirmed with the option…
rules.summary: When Delete is confirmed with the option to clear the key or to delete all values under it, the choice is accepted without further input
rules.detail: When Delete is confirmed with the option to clear the key or to delete all values under it, the choice is accepted without further input; no option is chosen when the dialog opens, and confirming with none chosen does nothing.

rules.headline: When the key name dialog is confirmed
rules.summary: When the key name dialog is confirmed, the typed name is returned unchecked; when it is cancelled, an empty name is returned
rules.detail: When the key name dialog is confirmed, the typed name is returned unchecked; when it is cancelled, an empty name is returned, so an empty typed name and a cancel look the same to the caller.

rules.headline: When Delete is confirmed with the option…
rules.summary: "; with a name, the choice is accepted.
rules.detail: When Delete is confirmed with the option to delete one value and the value name is empty, it is refused and the person is told "You must enter a value name."; with a name, the choice is accepted.

rules.headline: Section dialog lets a person choose only…
rules.detail: The section dialog lets a person choose only the sections the caller allows: User and Computer are each usable only when enabled by the caller.

rules.headline: When the guess fails
rules.detail: When the guess fails, the person is only warned "An error occurred while trying to guess the prefix." and the prefix stays empty.

rules.headline: Export to a registry script is refused
rules.summary: Export to a registry script is refused until a file name is given
rules.detail: Export to a registry script is refused until a file name is given; the person is told "Please specify a filename and path for the exported REG."

rules.headline: Value name box in the delete dialog can…
rules.detail: The value name box in the delete dialog can be typed in only while the option to delete one value is chosen.

rules.headline: Pressing Escape closes Import REG as cancelled
rules.detail: Pressing Escape closes Import REG as cancelled.

rules.headline: When the registry script is written
rules.summary: " and the dialog stays open.
rules.detail: When the registry script is written, the person is told "REG exported successfully." and the dialog closes; on any failure they are told only "Failed to export REG!" and the dialog stays open.

rules.headline: Special deletion entries in a policy file…
rules.summary: <name>" as "Delete value" with the name, and entries starting "**delvals" as "Delete all values". They cannot be edited or deleted.
rules.detail: Special deletion entries in a policy file are listed as such: "**deletevalues" as "Delete values" with its data, "**del.<name>" as "Delete value" with the name, and entries starting "**delvals" as "Delete all values". They cannot be edited or deleted.

rules.headline: Import is refused with "Please specify a REG…
rules.summary: " when no prefix is given.
rules.detail: Import is refused with "Please specify a REG file to import." when no file is named, and with "Please specify the prefix used to fully qualify paths in the REG file." when no prefix is given.

rules.headline: Import loads the REG file with the prefix…
rules.summary: Import loads the REG file with the prefix and applies it straight to the chosen policy source
rules.detail: Import loads the REG file with the prefix and applies it straight to the chosen policy source; on any failure the person is told only "Failed to import the REG file."

rules.headline: When a typed hexadecimal number is too large…
rules.summary: When a typed hexadecimal number is too large to fit, the value is set to the largest allowed value; text
rules.detail: When a typed hexadecimal number is too large to fit, the value is set to the largest allowed value; text that is not a hexadecimal number leaves the value unchanged.

rules.headline: Ordinary values are listed with their content
rules.summary: Ordinary values are listed with their content: lists of text joined by spaces, text as it is, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers in decimal
rules.detail: Ordinary values are listed with their content: lists of text joined by spaces, text as it is, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers in decimal, binary data as hexadecimal bytes separated by spaces. Other kinds show no content.

rules.headline: Pressing Done (or Enter) closes the raw policy…
rules.summary: Pressing Done (or Enter) closes the raw policy editor as accepted, and pressing Escape closes it as cancelled; there is no Cancel button.
rules.detail: Pressing Done (or Enter) closes the raw policy editor as accepted, and pressing Escape closes it as cancelled; there is no Cancel button. The caller ignores the answer, so every change made in the editor stays on the loaded policy source either way, to reach disk only when policies are saved.

rules.headline: Category appears in the tree only when it…
rules.summary: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule
rules.detail: A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule; each shown category gets an icon by its kind and carries its visible subcategories below it, and the tree is sorted.

rules.headline: After the category tree is rebuilt…
rules.summary: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category
rules.detail: After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category, policy or highlighted item is selected and the information pane shows the empty state.

rules.headline: New key name is refused with "The key…
rules.detail: A new key name is refused with "The key name is not valid." when it contains a backslash.

rules.headline: When the list is rebuilt
rules.summary: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is
rules.detail: When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is, it sits in the category shown and passes the visibility rule; otherwise nothing is selected. Then, if the policy is in the same category and the list still has that many rows, the earlier top row is put back, so the policy is not guaranteed to stay in view.

rules.headline: New key name is refused with "The key…
rules.summary: " when a key of that name, ignoring case, already exists under the same parent.
rules.detail: A new key name is refused with "The key name is already taken." when a key of that name, ignoring case, already exists under the same parent.

rules.headline: Adding a key does nothing when the name…
rules.summary: Adding a key does nothing when the name is left empty or the dialog is cancelled; otherwise the key is created under the selected key
rules.detail: Adding a key does nothing when the name is left empty or the dialog is cancelled; otherwise the key is created under the selected key, or at the top level when nothing is selected, as an empty key, and is selected in the list.

rules.headline: Right pane lists the chosen category in this…
rules.summary: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent
rules.detail: The right pane lists the chosen category in this order: an "Up: <parent name>" row marked "Parent" when the category has a parent, then visible subcategories by name, then visible policies by name. Each policy row shows its state and its comment text.

rules.headline: Editing a value offers a text
rules.summary: Editing a value offers a text, number or list-of-text dialog by kind: text kinds (plain and expandable) a text box
rules.detail: Editing a value offers a text, number or list-of-text dialog by kind: text kinds (plain and expandable) a text box, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers a number box, lists of text a multi-line box. Any other kind, such as binary, is refused with "This value kind is not supported." and nothing changes. Cancelling the dialog leaves the value as it was.

rules.headline: Category tree selection follows the category shown…
rules.detail: The category tree selection follows the category shown in the right pane.

rules.headline: When nothing is selected
rules.detail: When nothing is selected, the title and support lines are hidden and the pane reads "Select an item to see its description.".

rules.headline: For a selected policy the information pane shows…
rules.summary: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name
rules.detail: For a selected policy the information pane shows its title, "(no requirements information)" when it has no support rule or "Requirements:" plus the support name, and its explanation. A notice that the policy is a preference appears only for preferences.

rules.headline: Adding a value to the selected key lets…
rules.summary: Adding a value to the selected key lets the person choose a name and one of five kinds; the starting data is empty text, zero
rules.detail: Adding a value to the selected key lets the person choose a name and one of five kinds; the starting data is empty text, zero, or an empty list by kind, and the value is stored only if the person then confirms its data. A value of the same name in that key is replaced without warning.

rules.headline: For a selected or highlighted category the pane…
rules.summary: " ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.
rules.detail: For a selected or highlighted category the pane shows its title, "This category contains N policies and M subcategories." ("The selected category" when highlighted but not opened) and its explanation. The counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.

rules.headline: Category is orphaned when it has no parent…
rules.detail: A category is orphaned when it has no parent among the loaded definitions although its definition names one.

rules.headline: Category is empty when it holds no subcategories…
rules.detail: A category is empty when it holds no subcategories and no policies at all, counting hidden ones.

rules.headline: Deleting a key offers three choices
rules.summary: Deleting a key offers three choices, and OK does nothing until one is chosen; cancelling or Escape changes nothing.
rules.detail: Deleting a key offers three choices, and OK does nothing until one is chosen; cancelling or Escape changes nothing. Clear everything removes all values and marks the key cleared. Clear first marks the key cleared and puts back only its existing direct values with ordinary content; deletion entries already in that key are lost and values of sub-keys are not put back. Delete one value is refused with "You must enter a value name." when the name is empty; otherwise any value of that name, whether or not it exists, is removed and replaced by a deletion entry.

rules.headline: Category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned
rules.detail: A category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned, then empty, then normal.

rules.headline: Policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference
rules.detail: A policy's icon is chosen in this order: preference, then plain when it has no configurable elements, then "extra configuration" when it has some.

rules.headline: Category is visible when empty categories are switched…
rules.summary: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on.
rules.detail: A category is visible when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is visible only if it has at least one visible policy or one visible subcategory.

rules.headline: Deleting a single value from the list does…
rules.summary: " followed by the value name, which removes the value on the machine when policies are applied.
rules.detail: Deleting a single value from the list does not erase it from the file: it is replaced by a deletion entry named "**del." followed by the value name, which removes the value on the machine when policies are applied.

rules.headline: Policy is visible only if it applies…
rules.summary: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both).
rules.detail: A policy is visible only if it applies to a chosen area (user, computer or both). With "Only Filtered Policies" on, it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to; passing for either one is enough.

rules.headline: Forgetting a key asks "Are you sure you…
rules.summary: Forgetting a key asks "Are you sure you want to remove this key and all its contents?" and, on Yes, removes the key
rules.detail: Forgetting a key asks "Are you sure you want to remove this key and all its contents?" and, on Yes, removes the key, all its sub-keys, every value and every clearing mark from the file with no deletion left behind; No changes nothing. Forgetting a value removes the value and its deletion entry the same way.

rules.headline: When a view setting changes
rules.summary: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category
rules.detail: When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if the move happened or the policy is now hidden, then rebuilds the tree and list. A policy kept after the move appears in the information pane only: rebuilding the list reselects the category in the tree, which clears the selection, so its row is not highlighted.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to both areas shows its common state followed by "(2)" when both match, the computer state followed by "(C)" when only the user is Not Configured, the user state followed by "(U)" when only the computer is Not Configured, and "Mixed" otherwise.

rules.headline: Editing a value replaces its data…
rules.detail: Editing a value replaces its data with the confirmed new data and keeps its name and kind; the value stays selected.

rules.headline: With both areas shown, a policy
rules.summary: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user.
rules.detail: With both areas shown, a policy that applies to one area shows that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user. With a single area shown, only that area's state is shown, without a suffix.

rules.headline: When nothing is selected in the policy file's…
rules.detail: When nothing is selected in the policy file's list, only Add key and Export are available; Add value, Delete value, Edit and Forget are unavailable.

rules.headline: Policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled"
rules.summary: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"
rules.detail: A policy's state in one area reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown"; the computer source is read for the computer area and the user source for any other.

rules.headline: When a key is selected in the list
rules.detail: When a key is selected in the list, Add key, Add value, Delete value, Forget and Export are available, and Edit is unavailable.

rules.headline: When a value is selected in the list
rules.summary: When a value is selected in the list, only Forget is always available; Add key, Add value and Export are unavailable
rules.detail: When a value is selected in the list, only Forget is always available; Add key, Add value and Export are unavailable, and Edit and Delete value are available only when the value is not already a delete marker.

rules.headline: With both areas shown
rules.summary: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one
rules.detail: With both areas shown, the comment column is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one, and otherwise shows the single comment.

rules.headline: Export dialog starts with the selected key…
rules.summary: The export dialog starts with the selected key as its source branch, or empty when nothing is selected.
rules.detail: The export dialog starts with the selected key as its source branch, or empty when nothing is selected. The branch can be typed over, and the export uses the text in the box at the time: an empty box exports all of the policy file.

rules.headline: Policy's comment in one area is empty when
rules.summary: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy
rules.detail: A policy's comment in one area is empty when that source has no comment file or holds no comment for the policy, and otherwise the saved text.

rules.headline: Policy is a preference, not a managed policy
rules.detail: A policy is a preference, not a managed policy, when it names a registry key outside the three policy locations: software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies and system\currentcontrolset\policies.

rules.headline: Filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed…
rules.detail: A filter on managed policies hides preferences when managed policies are wanted, and hides managed policies when preferences are wanted.

rules.headline: Policy passes the filter only when it passes…
rules.detail: A policy passes the filter only when it passes every active part of it.

rules.headline: Filter on state keeps only policies whose state…
rules.detail: A filter on state keeps only policies whose state in the checked area is Configured (Enabled or Disabled), Not Configured, Disabled or Enabled, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on comments keeps only policies
rules.detail: A filter on comments keeps only policies that have a non-empty comment in the checked area, or only those that have none, as chosen.

rules.headline: Filter on products keeps only policies supported…
rules.summary: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products
rules.detail: A filter on products keeps only policies supported by the chosen products, honouring the options to match any product and to include policies with blank support.

rules.headline: Policy applies to an area when its definition…
rules.detail: A policy applies to an area when its definition declares that area; a policy declared for both applies to each.

rules.headline: Exporting uses a source backed by a POL…
rules.summary: Exporting uses a source backed by a POL file as is.
rules.detail: Exporting uses a source backed by a POL file as is. A registry-backed source (a chosen registry key or a loaded user hive file) is rebuilt as a new POL from the three policy locations: software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies and system\currentcontrolset\policies. Any other source type is rejected, which no known source type reaches.

rules.headline: When a POL is built from a registry-backed…
rules.summary: When a POL is built from a registry-backed source
rules.detail: When a POL is built from a registry-backed source, every value and every sub-key under each of the three policy locations is copied with its own data type, with environment variables left unexpanded. A location missing from the registry stops the copy with an unhandled error.

rules.headline: Importing a POL file applies it…
rules.summary: Importing a POL file applies it to the source the person chooses (user or computer). ". Nothing reaches disk until the person saves.
rules.detail: Importing a POL file applies it to the source the person chooses (user or computer). A file that cannot be read gives "The POL file could not be loaded." and changes nothing; success gives "POL import successful.". Nothing reaches disk until the person saves.

rules.headline: Exporting a POL file writes the chosen area's…
rules.detail: Exporting a POL file writes the chosen area's policy source as a POL file; the person sees "POL exported successfully." or "The POL file could not be saved.".

rules.headline: Raw POL editing is available only…
rules.summary: "; the area chosen is limited to POL-backed sources.
rules.detail: Raw POL editing is available only when the user or computer source is backed by a POL file, otherwise the person is told "Neither loaded source is backed by a POL file."; the area chosen is limited to POL-backed sources.

rules.headline: First time raw POL editing is used
rules.summary: The first time raw POL editing is used, the person must accept "Caution! This tool is for very advanced users.
rules.detail: The first time raw POL editing is used, the person must accept "Caution! This tool is for very advanced users. Improper modifications may result in inconsistencies in policies' states." (Yes continues and records the acceptance; No cancels and asks again next time).

rules.headline: Exporting to a registry file (REG) hands…
rules.summary: Exporting to a registry file (REG) hands the policy source of the area the person chooses, as a POL, to the export dialog.
rules.detail: Exporting to a registry file (REG) hands the policy source of the area the person chooses, as a POL, to the export dialog. An unsupported source raises an unhandled error, unlike Export POL, which tells the person.

rules.headline: Importing a registry file (REG) applies it…
rules.detail: Importing a registry file (REG) applies it to the policy source of the area the person chooses and refreshes the view.

rules.headline: Text of a policy description is tidied…
rules.summary: The text of a policy description is tidied for display
rules.detail: The text of a policy description is tidied for display: leading and trailing spaces are removed from every line and blank space at the end of the text is dropped.

rules.headline: Policy's lists of on-values and off-values count…
rules.summary: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present
rules.detail: A policy's lists of on-values and off-values count as enabled or disabled evidence for each value in them that is present, using the list's own key when it names one.

rules.headline: Policy with a registry value of its own…
rules.summary: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value
rules.detail: A policy with a registry value of its own counts as enabled evidence when that value holds its 'on' value, which is the number 1 when the template gives none, and as disabled evidence when it holds its 'off' value or is marked for deletion when the template gives none.

rules.headline: Policy file is refused when it does not…
rules.detail: A policy file is refused when it does not start with the 'PReg' signature, with the message 'Missing PReg signature'.

rules.headline: Policy file is refused when its format version…
rules.detail: A policy file is refused when its format version is not 1, with the message 'Unknown (newer) version of POL format'.

rules.headline: For a policy's list elements
rules.summary: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list
rules.detail: For a policy's list elements, a marked-for-deletion list counts as one deleted element, and a list that holds any values counts as a present element and cancels that deletion.

rules.headline: Blank lines and lines starting with a semicolon…
rules.detail: Blank lines and lines starting with a semicolon in a REG file are ignored.

rules.headline: REG file is refused when its first line…
rules.detail: A REG file is refused when its first line is not 'Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00', with the message 'Incorrect REG signature'.

rules.headline: For a checkbox element
rules.summary: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element.
rules.detail: For a checkbox element: a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element. Otherwise, each present off value (or off-list value) counts a tenth of a deleted element, and each present on value (or on-list value) counts one present element. A checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence, even if it holds 1.

rules.headline: When a policy file is read
rules.detail: When a policy file is read, an extra empty character after the value name, as Microsoft's documentation allows, is skipped.

rules.headline: REG key header starting with a minus sign…
rules.detail: A REG key header starting with a minus sign marks the whole key for removal. Otherwise it opens a key whose values follow.

rules.headline: When a policy file is read…
rules.summary: When a policy file is read and the same key and value name occur twice, the later entry wins.
rules.detail: When a policy file is read and the same key and value name occur twice, the later entry wins. Key and value names are matched without regard to letter case, and the first spelling seen is kept for saving.

rules.headline: For any other element (number, text, choice
rules.summary: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value
rules.detail: For any other element (number, text, choice, multi-line text), a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value that is present counts as a present element.

rules.headline: REG file value line starting…
rules.detail: A REG file value line starting with an at sign is the key's default value, with an empty name.

rules.headline: In a REG file
rules.summary: In a REG file, a value written as a bare minus sign is a value to delete.
rules.detail: In a REG file, a value written as a bare minus sign is a value to delete. A quoted value is text, 'dword:' is a 32-bit number in hexadecimal, and 'hex' is bytes, typed by the number in brackets or binary if none. Data in none of these forms is kept as a value with no data and no type, with no error, and applying it writes an empty value or fails.

rules.headline: If any element is present
rules.summary: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence
rules.detail: If any element is present, the elements add their count to the enabled evidence; only when none is present do deleted elements add to the disabled evidence.

rules.headline: Policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled…
rules.summary: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way
rules.detail: A policy is Enabled when enabled evidence exceeds disabled evidence, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way, and Unclear when both are equal and above zero.

rules.headline: When a policy file is saved
rules.detail: When a policy file is saved, entries are written in alphabetical order, so a key-clearing marker is always written before the values it clears.

rules.headline: Value counts as present when
rules.summary: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number
rules.detail: A value counts as present when: for a deletion marker, it is marked for deletion; for a number, it exists as a whole number and equals the expected number; for text, it exists as text and equals the expected text. A value of the wrong kind is not present.

rules.headline: When a value is marked for deletion…
rules.summary: When a value is marked for deletion in a policy file, any value or marker already held under that name is dropped first.
rules.detail: When a value is marked for deletion in a policy file, any value or marker already held under that name is dropped first. A deletion marker holding the number 32, as Microsoft does, is added unless the value is already marked or its key is cleared.

rules.headline: When a value is forgotten in a policy…
rules.summary: When a value is forgotten in a policy file, both the value and its deletion marker are removed
rules.detail: When a value is forgotten in a policy file, both the value and its deletion marker are removed, so the policy reverts to not saying anything about it.

rules.headline: When a value is set in a policy…
rules.summary: When a value is set in a policy file, it replaces any value already held under that name.
rules.detail: When a value is set in a policy file, it replaces any value already held under that name. A deletion marker for the name is not removed.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as present…
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as present only if it is stored and not marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Reading a value from a policy file gives…
rules.detail: Reading a value from a policy file gives nothing when the value is absent or marked for deletion.

rules.headline: When a REG file is written
rules.summary: When a REG file is written, a default value is shown as an at sign, and quotes and backslashes in names and text are escaped.
rules.detail: When a REG file is written, a default value is shown as an at sign, and quotes and backslashes in names and text are escaped. Text is written as quoted text and a 32-bit number as 'dword:' with eight hexadecimal digits. Every other type, including 64-bit numbers, expandable text and multiple strings, is written as hex bytes. Each carries its type number as hex(n), except plain binary, which is written as hex. Lines wrap before column 78 with a trailing backslash.

rules.headline: Value in a policy file counts as marked…
rules.summary: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker
rules.detail: A value in a policy file counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker names it, when the key has a clear-all marker, or when a delete-values list for the key names it, regardless of case. Entries are examined in sorted order, and a value whose name sorts after the marker is stored as present and cancels the deletion, whenever it was written and whichever marker kind came before.

rules.headline: Keys marked for removal are written…
rules.detail: Keys marked for removal are written to a REG file with a leading minus sign and values marked for deletion as a bare minus sign.

rules.headline: Listing the values of a key…
rules.detail: Listing the values of a key in a policy file leaves out the marker entries unless the caller asks for them.

rules.headline: When a policy file's changes are applied…
rules.summary: ' plus a value name deletes that value, using the lower-case key and value names.
rules.detail: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry named '**del.' plus a value name deletes that value, using the lower-case key and value names.

rules.headline: When a policy file's changes are applied…
rules.summary: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry starting '**delvals' clears the whole key, using the lower-case key name.
rules.detail: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry starting '**delvals' clears the whole key, using the lower-case key name. Entries are applied in sorted order, so clear-all entries come before values. Clearing a live registry key removes only that key's own values.

rules.headline: When a policy file's changes are applied…
rules.detail: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry named '**deletevalues' deletes each value in its semicolon-separated list, using lower-case names.

rules.headline: When a policy file's changes are applied…
rules.summary: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source
rules.detail: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry starting '**deletekeys' clears each key named in its semicolon-separated list under the entry's key, using lower-case names. Clearing removes only that key's own values, not its subkeys.

rules.headline: When a policy file's changes are applied…
rules.summary: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry is saved only if it has a non-empty value name
rules.detail: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, an entry is saved only if it has a non-empty value name that does not start with '**'. Other marker-style entries and entries with an empty value name are skipped without notice. A saved value keeps its original letter case and type.

rules.headline: When a newer policy file is applied over…
rules.summary: When a newer policy file is applied over an older one
rules.detail: When a newer policy file is applied over an older one, values the old file held and the new one dropped are forgotten in the target, but only if they sit under the three policy branches of the registry.

rules.headline: Applying a whole policy file to a source…
rules.detail: Applying a whole policy file to a source applies it as the difference from an empty file, so nothing is forgotten.

rules.headline: When a policy file is clearing a key
rules.detail: When a policy file is clearing a key, all values and markers under the key are dropped and a single clear-all marker is stored.

rules.headline: REG key name is shortened by the prefix…
rules.detail: A REG key name is shortened by the prefix only when it starts with it, regardless of case. A prefix always ends in a backslash.

rules.headline: When a key's clearance is forgotten…
rules.detail: When a key's clearance is forgotten in a policy file, every clear-all marker for that key is removed.

rules.headline: Key name in a policy file is listed…
rules.detail: A key name in a policy file is listed as a subkey only once, regardless of case, and the requested key itself is never listed.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for asking whether a value is present: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for reading a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for checking whether a value will be deleted: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for listing a key's values: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: When a value is saved into a REG…
rules.summary: When a value is saved into a REG file, it is ignored if a source branch is set and its key lies outside that branch.
rules.detail: When a value is saved into a REG file, it is ignored if a source branch is set and its key lies outside that branch. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Any value already stored under that name is replaced.

rules.headline: Text read from a policy file stops…
rules.detail: Text read from a policy file stops at its first empty character, and a multiple-string value ends at its first empty string.

rules.headline: REG file cannot be used as a source…
rules.summary: A REG file cannot be used as a source for forgetting a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'.
rules.detail: A REG file cannot be used as a source for forgetting a value: the request fails with 'not implemented'. Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a REG file fails this way for any dropped value under a policy branch.

rules.headline: Text stored in a policy file is written…
rules.detail: Text stored in a policy file is written in two-byte characters followed by a closing empty character.

rules.headline: When a value is deleted in a REG…
rules.summary: When a value is deleted in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it
rules.detail: When a value is deleted in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it, or if the key is already marked for removal. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Otherwise the value is recorded as deleted.

rules.headline: When a key is cleared in a REG…
rules.summary: When a key is cleared in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it.
rules.detail: When a key is cleared in a REG file, the request is ignored if a source branch is set and the key lies outside it. When no branch is set, every key is accepted. Otherwise the key's earlier entries are replaced by a key-removal entry.

rules.headline: 32-bit number is stored in a policy file…
rules.detail: A 32-bit number is stored in a policy file as 4 bytes, lowest byte first.

rules.headline: When a REG file is applied…
rules.summary: When a REG file is applied to a source, a key marked for removal is cleared
rules.detail: When a REG file is applied to a source, a key marked for removal is cleared, a value marked for deletion is deleted and any other value is saved. A key name starting with the prefix is applied without it. A key not starting with the prefix is applied with its full original name, so the registry source would create a key of that name. The source branch limit is not checked.

rules.headline: 64-bit number is stored in a policy file…
rules.detail: A 64-bit number is stored in a policy file as 8 bytes, lowest byte first.

rules.headline: Branch name given as the source…
rules.detail: A branch name given as the source of a REG export has any trailing backslash removed.

rules.headline: Prefix of a REG file is guessed…
rules.summary: The prefix of a REG file is guessed from its first key only.
rules.detail: The prefix of a REG file is guessed from its first key only. For a key starting with 'HKEY_USERS\' it is that hive plus the user identifier. For any other key, including HKEY_CURRENT_USER, it is the hive name alone. A first key with no further backslash gives an empty prefix. A file with no keys gets 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\'.

rules.headline: Multiple-string value is stored as its strings…
rules.detail: A multiple-string value is stored as its strings each followed by an empty character, with one more empty character closing the list.

rules.headline: REG file is reported as holding default values…
rules.detail: A REG file is reported as holding default values when any value has an empty name.

rules.headline: Stored policy file value is read back…
rules.summary: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers
rules.detail: A stored policy file value is read back as text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers, a list of strings for multiple strings, and raw bytes for every other type.

rules.headline: Value written to a policy file is stored…
rules.summary: A value written to a policy file is stored as text, expandable text
rules.detail: A value written to a policy file is stored as text, expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number or a multiple string by its stated type. Every other type is stored as raw bytes with that type.

rules.headline: When a value is deleted in the live…
rules.detail: When a value is deleted in the live registry and its key does not exist, nothing happens. A missing value is not an error.

rules.headline: In the live registry
rules.detail: In the live registry, 'forgetting' a value deletes it, because the registry cannot remember a pending deletion.

rules.headline: When a number is saved to the live…
rules.summary: When a number is saved to the live registry
rules.detail: When a number is saved to the live registry, an unsigned 32-bit or 64-bit number is converted to the signed number the registry stores with the same bits, and the key is created if missing.

rules.headline: When a policy lists no supported-on information
rules.summary: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies.
rules.detail: When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies. The same applies to a support entry that names no known product.

rules.headline: Value in the live registry counts as present…
rules.summary: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty
rules.detail: A value in the live registry counts as present when its key exists and, unless the value name is empty, the key lists a value of that name, regardless of case. An empty name means the key itself.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product counts as met…
rules.summary: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases.
rules.detail: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases. The entry is not a version range and that exact product is among the chosen products. Or the product has versions beneath it, and any of those versions or their sub-products is chosen, even when the product itself is not.

rules.headline: Support entry for a product
rules.summary: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product
rules.detail: A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product that is not itself chosen, counts as met when any version in its range, or a sub-product directly beneath one, is chosen. The range runs from the entry's minimum (0 if none) to its maximum (the highest version if none). A range entry never matches on its own product, and a product with no versions beneath it never matches this way.

rules.headline: Reading a value from the live registry gives…
rules.summary: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing.
rules.detail: Reading a value from the live registry gives nothing when the key is missing. Signed numbers are returned as the unsigned numbers policies use, and environment variables in text are not expanded.

rules.headline: Support definition met a second time anywhere…
rules.summary: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied.
rules.detail: A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied. Two entries that point at the same definition, with no cycle, make the second one not met.

rules.headline: When the caller asks for 'any' matching
rules.summary: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met
rules.detail: When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met, and any other definition needs one entry met. When the caller does not ask for 'any', every definition, all-of included, is met by one entry. A definition with no entries, or none met, is met only when all are required. Plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.

rules.headline: Live registry never reports a value as marked…
rules.detail: The live registry never reports a value as marked for deletion.

rules.headline: Registry key counts as a policy key…
rules.summary: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one
rules.detail: A registry key counts as a policy key when it is one of the three policy branches (software\policies, software\microsoft\windows\currentversion\policies, system\currentcontrolset\policies) or lies below one, regardless of case.

rules.headline: Clearing a key in the live registry deletes…
rules.detail: Clearing a key in the live registry deletes every value in it but leaves the key and its subkeys. Forgetting a key's clearance does nothing.

actions.headline: Closes the key name dialog as cancelled…
actions.detail: Closes the key name dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.headline: Closes the list-of-strings dialog as cancelled when Escape…
actions.detail: Closes the list-of-strings dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.detail: Reports the chosen section (user or computer) and closes the dialog as accepted

actions.headline: Puts the cursor in the key name box…
actions.detail: Puts the cursor in the key name box with its text selected when the dialog appears.

actions.headline: Closes the new value dialog as cancelled…
actions.detail: Closes the new value dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.headline: Switches the number box between decimal and hexadecimal…
actions.detail: Switches the number box between decimal and hexadecimal display.

actions.headline: Closes the string dialog as cancelled when Escape…
actions.detail: Closes the string dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.headline: Lets the person pick a REG file…
actions.detail: Lets the person pick a REG file and guesses the key prefix from it.

actions.headline: Accepts the delete dialog when a choice…
actions.detail: Accepts the delete dialog when a choice is made and asks for a value name when deleting one value.

actions.headline: Lets the person pick the .reg file…
actions.detail: Lets the person pick the .reg file to write

actions.detail: Closes the dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed

actions.detail: Closes the number dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.detail: Closes the dialog as cancelled when Escape is pressed

actions.detail: Writes the chosen branch of the policy file to a .reg file

actions.headline: Closes the delete dialog as cancelled when Escape…

actions.headline: Shows the value as hexadecimal text when hexadecimal…
actions.detail: Shows the value as hexadecimal text when hexadecimal mode is on, otherwise leaves display to the standard control.

actions.headline: Enables the value name box only
actions.detail: Enables the value name box only while the delete-one-value option is chosen.

actions.detail: Closes the window as cancelled when Escape is pressed.

actions.headline: Loads the chosen REG file with its prefix…
actions.detail: Loads the chosen REG file with its prefix and applies it to the policy source.

actions.headline: Reads typed hexadecimal text into the value…
actions.detail: Reads typed hexadecimal text into the value in hexadecimal mode, otherwise leaves it to the standard control.

actions.headline: Closes the editor window with an OK result
actions.detail: Closes the editor window with an OK result; the changes were already applied to the policy source as each was made.

actions.headline: Closes the editor window with a Cancel result…
actions.detail: Closes the editor window with a Cancel result when Escape is pressed; edits already made stay applied to the policy source.

actions.headline: Asks for a new key name
actions.detail: Asks for a new key name, checks it is valid and free, and adds the empty key to the policy file.

actions.headline: Asks for a value name and type
actions.detail: Asks for a value name and type, then its data, and adds the value under the selected key.

actions.headline: Marks a value for deletion
actions.detail: Marks a value for deletion, or clears or purges a selected key, as the person chooses.

actions.headline: Removes a key with its contents
actions.detail: Removes a key with its contents, or one value, from the policy file without leaving a deletion mark.

actions.headline: Asks for new data for the selected value…
actions.detail: Asks for new data for the selected value and stores it in the policy file.

actions.headline: Turns the editor buttons on or off…
actions.detail: Turns the editor buttons on or off to match the kind of item selected in the list.

actions.headline: Opens the registry file import dialog and refreshes…
actions.detail: Opens the registry file import dialog and refreshes the list if values were imported.

actions.headline: Opens the registry file export dialog…
actions.detail: Opens the registry file export dialog for the selected key.

actions.detail: Reads a chosen POL file and applies it to the user or computer policy source.

actions.detail: Writes a policy source out as a POL file.

concerns.name: Which registry branches count as policy
concerns.verdict: Business logic shared with other capabilities
concerns.purpose: Decides which registry branches are treated as policy, so the policy store and the main window know what to track and what to leave alone.

concerns.name: Reading and writing policy files
concerns.verdict: Business logic shared with other capabilities
concerns.purpose: Every place that changes or reads policies leans on the policy file code: loading, saving, listing values and forgetting a value.

risks.headline: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent.
risks.summary: Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace
risks.detail: A failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace inconsistent. Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace, so a failure leaves it empty. Several actions reset it; others do not.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names.
risks.summary: Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import
risks.detail: Applying a policy file's held changes to the live registry writes, deletes or clears whatever keys the file names. Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import, can change other registry keys.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden.
risks.summary: An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost
risks.detail: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden. An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost, and turning on the comment filter then fails with an unhandled error.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values.
risks.summary: A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.detail: Importing a REG file applies it key by key to the live policy source with no rollback, and a REG source cannot read or forget values. A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names.
risks.summary: The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.
risks.detail: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever source is open, live registry or policy file, with no check of the keys it names. The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.
risks.category: Someone can read or change what they should not

risks.headline: Policy files and REG files are saved by overwriting in place.
risks.summary: A failure partway leaves a truncated or damaged file, with no copy of the old one.
risks.detail: Policy files and REG files are saved by overwriting in place. A failure partway leaves a truncated or damaged file, with no copy of the old one.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: Saving a local or per-user policy writes the policy file first and the version file second.
risks.summary: A failure on the second step, or a malformed version line that truncates the version file, leaves new settings with an old or damaged version
risks.detail: Saving a local or per-user policy writes the policy file first and the version file second. A failure on the second step, or a malformed version line that truncates the version file, leaves new settings with an old or damaged version, which Group Policy clients use to detect change.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: The name of a value added in the raw policy editor is not checked.
risks.summary: An empty name hides the key's marker, and names
risks.detail: The name of a value added in the raw policy editor is not checked. An empty name hides the key's marker, and names that begin with deletion prefixes or equal the delete-values name are read back as deletion or clearing instructions.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does

risks.headline: When a download, install or export fails, the person sees only the step that failed, not the cause, with no retry.
risks.summary: A finished install can be reported as a failure when cleanup fails, leaving the new folder unloaded and unpacked files behind.
risks.detail: When a download, install or export fails, the person sees only the step that failed, not the cause, with no retry. A finished install can be reported as a failure when cleanup fails, leaving the new folder unloaded and unpacked files behind.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Changing or loading policy sources has no error handling.
risks.summary: Sources are replaced one by one, so a failure leaves a mix or an empty workspace with an unhandled error.
risks.detail: Changing or loading policy sources has no error handling. Sources are replaced one by one, so a failure leaves a mix or an empty workspace with an unhandled error. A start-up fallback still presets the failed sources, and a missing registry location stops a POL export.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Escape in the raw policy editor looks like a cancel, but every edit has already changed the loaded policy source and the caller ignores the answer.
risks.summary: Changes cannot be discarded except by not saving afterwards.
risks.detail: Escape in the raw policy editor looks like a cancel, but every edit has already changed the loaded policy source and the caller ignores the answer. Changes cannot be discarded except by not saving afterwards.
risks.category: Data can end up wrong, lost or inconsistent

risks.headline: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run.
risks.summary: Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.
risks.detail: If the program cannot create its settings key it carries on silently, so sources, folder, language and prompts revert each run. Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.
risks.category: Failures are hidden, lost or not retried

risks.headline: Reading a policy file trusts the length stored in each entry and the shape of the data.
risks.summary: A damaged or hostile file can demand huge memory or fail unexplained, and REG files report no line number on error.
risks.detail: Reading a policy file trusts the length stored in each entry and the shape of the data. A damaged or hostile file can demand huge memory or fail unexplained, and REG files report no line number on error.
risks.category: Input from outside is used without checks, so it can change what the code does
